instruction: GUI-only requirement: Complete the task entirely in the opened Blender graphical user interface. Do not open Command Prompt, PowerShell, Terminal, or any shell; do not run Python, bpy scripts, Text Editor scripts, Geometry Nodes exported scripts, or blender --background automation that directly generates or edits the deliverable files. Do not install or run helper add-ons that auto-build the required result. Use only Blender native GUI tools, menus, editors, and built-in save/export commands. Reference-File Path Normalization `scene.blend` contains three mesh objects `Plane_R`, `Plane_G`, and `Plane_B`. Each plane has a material with an Image Texture node bound to a 16x16 PNG (`red.png`, `green.png`, `blue.png`, stored in `/home/user/Desktop/textures/`). Crucially, each image datablock was loaded from an ABSOLUTE filesystem path, so `bpy.data.images[name].filepath` does NOT start with the Blender-relative `\\` prefix. Your task is to make every image path blend-relative and save the result to `answer.blend` (relative to the working directory). What to do 1. Use the opened `scene.blend`. 2. Save the blend to `answer.blend` FIRST (because `bpy.ops.file.make_paths_relative()` requires the .blend to already have a filepath on disk - that's what anchors the `\\` prefix). 3. Ensure the PNG assets are reachable from the new blend's location (e.g., copy `/home/user/Desktop/textures/*.png` into `/home/user/Desktop/textures/`). 4. Run `bpy.ops.file.make_paths_relative()`. This rewrites every absolute filepath (images, libraries, caches, etc.) into a blend-relative path starting with `\\`. 5. Save the blend again. Requirements: 1. `answer.blend` exists and opens as a valid Blender file. 2. There are at least three disk-backed (`source == 'FILE'`) image datablocks, excluding `Render Result` and `Viewer Node`. 3. Every such image's `filepath` starts with `\\` (blend-relative). 4. `bpy.path.abspath(image.filepath)` resolves to an existing file on disk for every image. 5. Every image loads (non-zero size, pixels accessible) after the blend is reopened - no missing images. 6. The three mesh objects `Plane_R`, `Plane_G`, `Plane_B` still exist, each with a material whose node tree includes an Image Texture node with an assigned image. Do not rename any object, material, or image datablock, and do not alter the shader graphs - only the image filepaths (and the location of the texture files on disk) should change.
